summary: Clackamas County tower 11 miles SSE of Estacada: 1949-50 tower collapsed under ice, rebuilt 1951 at 82 ft; cab removed 1970; a July 1985 entry shows a bare timber tower.

facts.design: 14-by-14 cab on an 82-foot tower after the 1951 rebuild (Forest Lookouts); firelookout.com gives an 84-foot wooden L-6 tower in the 1930s
facts.status_note: The Oregon list marks it gone, but a July 16, 1985 Forest Lookouts entry describes an 82-foot timber tower without a cab on the site; the current condition is not described

events.note: firelookout.com dates the first tower to the 1930s (84-foot wooden L-6); no other source gives an early date
Agency newsletter reports a new 70-foot tower in use; a district report gives an 82-foot tower with a 14-by-14 cab built that year
Tower went down January 14, 1950 under snow, ice and wind; a March report on the wreckage gives the cause as ice from a sleet storm
Rebuilt after a redesign for heavy icing; 1951 district report lists a 14-by-14 cab on an 82-foot tower
Lookout painted; metal roof replaced with cedar shingles
75-foot steel tower moved to Goat Mountain from Frog Lake Butte; the Frog Lake record says it was moved to serve as a radio tower
Cab taken off, floor left as a platform (survey note); firelookout.com says the structure was converted to an antenna tower
Forest Lookouts entry dated July 16, 1985 describes an 82-foot treated timber tower without a cab occupying the site

corrections.why: 21.3 m (70 ft) is the 1949 newsletter figure for the tower that collapsed in January 1950. The 1951 rebuild was 82 ft, about 25 m, the latest height given.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 84 ft (firelookout.com, 1930s), 70 ft (1949 newsletter), 80 ft (1950 press report of the collapse), 82 ft (1949 district report and 1951 report), 90 ft to the eaves (1953 survey), and a 75-ft steel tower (1967 move). The story says they disagree. height_m is set to the 1951 82-ft figure, about 25 m.

Firelookout.com dates the first tower to the 1930s. No other source gives an early date, and the 1949 newsletter calls the tower then in use new. The story reports the 1930s date as firelookout's claim.
Firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts name the Oregon Department of Forestry. The 1953 survey note uses the older name, Oregon State Forest Service. These are the same agency under different names.

The Oregon list marks the tower gone. An entry dated July 16, 1985 describes a timber tower standing on the site. The sources do not say when, or whether, that tower came down. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Heights disagree across six sources; height_m is proposed as 25.0 (82 ft from the 1951 rebuild) against the record's 21.3 m, which is the 1949 70-ft figure. Firelookout.com also gives a 1952 '20 ft L-4 tower' that no other source confirms; it was left out. Whether the 1967 steel tower and the 1985 timber tower are the same structure is not stated, so the story does not link them beyond the Frog Lake record. The Oregon list's 'gone' status conflicts with the July 16, 1985 entry; the editor may want to re-check the status field. No source describes staffing or fires at this site. Two online forum threads were seen in search results but not read, so the story makes no claim from them about current towers or access. Ownership is from a 1953 survey note and may be out of date. The 'today' section is limited to 1985 as the latest description.
